sections.title: 各地生日习俗（共享词库）
sections.passage: How do you celebrate your birthday? With a cake, a party for your friends and family? In some countries, birthday celebrations are really unusual. In China, a birthday child usually eats very long noodles with eggs. People never cut up the noodles (31) they are a symbol of long life, and eggs mean good luck. In some parts of India, when a child has their first birthday, their parents cut off all their hair. The child wears colorful clothes (32) gives chocolate to their friends. In Korea, they celebrate day number 100 (33) the child is born. Families make sure a birthday child gets many rice cakes with honey. When (34) child gets 100 rice cakes, this means they will live a happy and long life. When children in Denmark wake up (35) their birthday, they find gifts all around their beds. That’s why some of the children are so excited that they cannot fall asleep the night before!

sections.title: 真正的力量来自自己
sections.passage: Lele loved ping-pong and dreamed of winning a big match. One day, he was (36) to join the school ping-pong team, but he was worried about the big competition. After school, he went to visit his grandpa. They talked and Grandpa gave Lele a (37) . It was a trophy that Grandpa had won in a ping-pong competition when he was at school. “Wow! Thank you, Grandpa!” Lele said (38) . He felt confident the trophy would bring him luck. The day of the competition arrived. Lele’s grandpa came to cheer. Lele was really (39) , so he put the trophy on a bench where he could see it. The competition began. He felt (40) and confident and did so well that he got into the final. Just as the final round was about to start, he couldn’t see the trophy. Lele (41) in fear. The match began, but Lele couldn’t focus his attention. Then he heard his grandpa (42) , “Come on, Lele! You can do it!” He said to himself, “I can do this with or without the trophy!” Suddenly he felt strong again. He looked at his opponent (对手) and served a ball … Finally, Lele won the match. Lele (43) the trophy under the bench. It was there all the time! Then he thought maybe he had only won the match because of Grandpa’s (44) trophy. He ran over and asked Grandpa. Grandpa laughed, “Lele, you won because you tried your best. It was (45) , but you did it! Now go and get your own trophy. You deserve (应得) it!” Finally, Lele had won his own ping-pong trophy!

groups.label: B
groups.title: 为自然作出改变
groups.passage: Human actions are affecting the environment. We will lose more of the natural world if we don’t try to change things. Though it is difficult, we can make a difference. Each small change is important, and luckily more individuals (个人) and organizations are working on conservation (保 护) projects. Samson, an African fisherman, has become a voice for the ocean. He and the other fishermen realized they were catching fewer and fewer fish. They were overfishing. Working with the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), Samson learned they had to fish more carefully. He realized they shouldn’t catch so many young fish because if there are too few of them, there won’t be enough adult fish to reproduce. He believes protecting the ocean is everybody’s job. As he says, “Take your responsibilities and never think that you are alone.” In Florida, the Sea Turtle Conservancy (STC) noticed there were always plenty of single-use plastic items, like bottles and drinking straws (吸管), on the beaches. These items can hurt the ocean wildlife terribly. Straws are especially dangerous for turtles because they can get stuck in turtles’ noses and hurt them badly. So, the STC started the project “Where are the straws?” asking local restaurants to stop giving customers straws with their drinks. Now, restaurants will only give straws if customers ask for them, and they only give out paper straws. Those are just two examples of the many conservation efforts around the world today. They both show us that change is possible and that it can start with small actions. We are part of the problem. It’s time to be part of the solution

groups.label: C
groups.title: 课堂外学科学
groups.passage: Chile is a long and beautiful country with the ocean to the west and mountains to the east. Some of the villages are a very long way from the cities, and some of the schools are very small. It’s difficult for small schools to teach science because they don’t have enough teachers or equipment (设备). This is where the Science Bus project can help. The bus brings special science teachers, new ideas, and equipment to schools in different parts of the country. Sometimes, the children go inside the bus for their science classes or clubs. Sometimes, the teachers bring the equipment inside the school building. The children do experiments. The materials used in the experiments are easy to find — for example, recycled plastic bottles — so that the class teacher can repeat the experiments with the class after the bus leaves. The goal of the Science Bus is to bring science to children all over Chile. Since 2012, the bus has visited many schools in Chile, and hundreds of teachers have learned how to make their science classes fun and exciting. In other parts of the world, children can take part in events called Bioblitzes. During a Bioblitz, scientists, families, students, teachers, and other people work together to collect as many different kinds of plants and animals as possible in a certain place, such as a park or a forest. Bioblitzes are a fun way to help scientists and to discover more about the plants and animals around us. Science is important for all of us because it helps us understand our world. We can learn about science inside or outside of the classroom.

items.stem: Why do Chile’s small schools need the Science Bus?
options: They don’t have enough school buildings or clubs.
They are short of science teachers and equipment.
They need special materials to repeat experiments.
items.exp: 第二段明确说明缺科学教师和设备。

items.stem: What do people do during a Bioblitz?
items.exp: Bioblitz 活动收集植物和动物。

items.stem: What do the Science Bus and Bioblitzes have in common?
options: They are popular with children in Chile.
They choose science courses for schools.
items.exp: 两种活动都让学习科学有趣。

items.stem: What is the writer’s purpose in writing the text?
options: To encourage us to learn science.
To advise us to get close to nature.
To introduce Chile’s schools to us.
items.exp: 末段强调科学重要并可在课内外学习，意在鼓励学习科学。

sections.title: 积极面对生活（六选五）
sections.passage: Do you often have negative thoughts? Do you and your friends often complain (抱怨) about things? (58) .  Find the positive, however small. Bad things happen to all of us, but the most important thing is to focus on the positive. For example, next time you are caught in traffic, think how great it is that you can finish listening to your favorite music. If you don’t have much in your fridge, get creative and think of what you can invent with the ingredients (食材) you have. (59) .  Focus on now It’s easy to think too much about things that have already happened and to get worried about what will happen tomorrow. (60) . But remember, you can’t change the past, and no one can control the future, so the best thing is to focus on the present.  (61) . Being around negative people will make you feel negative, too. Spend time with people who will make you laugh and help you believe in yourself, not those that spend all day complaining. It’s hard to feel negative when you have positive people around you.  Be kind to others One of the best ways to make yourself feel good is to help others. (62) . Spending time helping other people can give you a better perspective (视角) on life and make you value what you have.
choices: Always remind yourself to work hard
It can be exciting to try something new
Find ways to volunteer in your community
The following can help you feel positive about life

sections.prompt: 老师 Lucy 鼓励大家记录课堂故事、班级活动、师生趣事等校园生活，共同编写 Our Stories。请以 A(n) ______ Story 为题写约80词短文：补全标题，写出发生的事情及感受。不得出现真实姓名和学校名。
points: 叙述一件校园故事，过程具体
sections.sample:
An Unforgettable Story
Last Friday, our class held an English story competition. I was nervous because it was my first time speaking in front of so many people. When I forgot a sentence, our English teacher smiled and encouraged me. My classmates clapped for me, too. I took a deep breath and continued my story. Although I did not win first prize, I felt proud of myself. This experience taught me that courage and support from others can help us overcome difficulties.
sections.exp: 范文为编写示例，非官方范文。以一般过去时写校园经历，补全标题并清楚表达感受。
